answer: A sock-puppet farm minting many identities pays full stake per token into a shared vault, and any duplicate pattern burns that stake. Each agent must stake a unique pigment-tagged identity token whose dye pattern is derived from hardware entropy, making duplicates detectably identical to peers. Legitimate agents also earn a plume score from attested work history, so fresh identities lack the plume weight needed for rewards, raising attacker cost above expected gain. From sa0016's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
